title: Times tables & division
blurb: A trick for each times family, the tricky-fact rhymes, and long division.

groups.name: What × means
steps: Order does not change the total: 4 groups of 3 is also 12.
groups.exception: Times is not plus. 3 × 4 is not 7. Anything times 0 is 0, and anything times 1 stays the same.

doubles.phrase: ×2 is double. ×4 is double-double. ×8 is double-double-double.
doubles.exception: Count your doubles. Doubling twice is ×4, not ×8. And ×6 is not a doubling family: it is ×5 plus one more group.

steps: Multiply by 10: put a 0 on the end.
fives.exception: An even number of fives ends in 0. An odd number ends in 5. If your answer ends in anything else, check again.

nines.phrase: Fold the finger. Left fingers are tens, right fingers are ones.
nines.also: The digits always add to nine.
steps: 6 fingers on the left, 3 on the right: 63.
nines.exception: The fingers work up to 9 × 10. For 9 × 12, do 10 × 12 and take away 12. And 9 × 0 is 0.

rhymes.name: Tricky facts
rhymes.phrase: Five, six, seven, eight: fifty-six is seven times eight.
rhymes.also: I ate and ate and got sick on the floor: eight times eight is sixty-four.
steps: Six times six, magic tricks: thirty-six.
I know now and you do too: six times seven is forty-two.
Six and eight went on a date, came back as forty-eight.
Seven and seven are doing fine: forty-nine.
Five, six, seven, eight: fifty-six is seven times eight.
I ate and ate and got sick on the floor: eight times eight is sixty-four.
rhymes.exception: A rhyme is a hook, not the reason. If you forget it, build from a fact you know: 7 × 8 is 7 × 7 plus one more 7, which is 49 + 7 = 56.

elevens.name: ×11 for two digits
elevens.phrase: Split the digits. Park their sum in the middle.
elevens.exception: If the middle sum is 10 or more, carry the 1 to the left digit. 85 × 11: 8 + 5 = 13, so 8 + 1 = 9, then 3, then 5: 935.

longdiv.name: Long division
longdiv.also: Dad, Mom, Sister, Brother, and Rover the dog repeats it.
steps: Divide: how many times does it fit?
Multiply: that answer times the divisor.
Bring down the next digit, then repeat.
longdiv.exception: What is left must be smaller than the divisor. If it is not, your divide step was too small. If the divisor does not fit at all, write a 0 in the answer before you bring down.

divis.name: Divisibility rules
divis.phrase: Last digit for 2, 5, and 10. Add the digits for 3 and 9. Last two digits for 4. Six needs 2 and 3.
steps: 5: it ends in 0 or 5. 10: it ends in 0.
3 or 9: add the digits. If the sum divides by 3 (or 9), so does the number.
4: the last two digits divide by 4.
6: it passes the test for 2 and the test for 3.
divis.exception: Adding the digits works only for 3 and 9, not for 4 or 7. Six needs both tests: 15 passes 3 but is odd, so it fails 6.

primes.name: Factors, multiples, and primes
primes.phrase: Factors are few, multiples are many. A prime has just two factors: 1 and itself.
primes.also: Factors fit into a number. Multiples are what you get when you times it.
steps: Factors of 12: numbers that divide 12 exactly: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12.
Prime: exactly two factors, like 7 (1 and 7).
Composite: more than two factors, like 9 (1, 3, 9).
primes.exception: 1 is not prime: it has only one factor. 2 is the only even prime. Odd does not mean prime: 9, 15, and 21 are composite.

areaper.name: Area and perimeter
areaper.phrase: Perimeter is the fence around. Area is the carpet inside.
steps: Perimeter: add all four sides, or 2 × (length + width).
Perimeter is a length (cm). Area is squares (cm²).
areaper.exception: Don’t mix them up: a 5 by 3 rectangle has a fence of 16 but a carpet of 15. Two shapes with the same area can have different perimeters.

roundbig.name: Rounding big numbers
roundbig.phrase: Underline the place. Look next door. Five or more, raise the score.
roundbig.also: Four or less, let it rest.
steps: Underline the digit in the place you want.
Look at the digit next door, on its right.
5 or more: the underlined digit goes up 1. 4 or less: it stays.
roundbig.exception: If the underlined digit is a 9 and it goes up, it rolls over: 3,960 to the nearest hundred is 4,000. Don’t round in steps: 3,449 → 3,450 → 3,500 is wrong. It is 3,400.

equivfr.name: Equivalent fractions
equivfr.phrase: What you do to the top, you do to the bottom.
steps: Multiply (or divide) the top by it.
Do the same to the bottom. It looks different, but it is the same amount.
equivfr.exception: Only × and ÷ work. Adding the same number to the top and bottom changes the amount: 1/2 is not 2/3.

times10.phrase: Each zero slides the digits one place left.
times10.also: × 10: one place. × 100: two places. × 1000: three places. Zeros fill the empty seats.
steps: Slide every digit that many places to the left.
Fill the empty seats with zeros.
times10.exception: Count the zeros in the 10, 100, or 1000 only. 40 × 100 is 4,000: the 0 in 40 moves too, and two new zeros join it.

roman-iview.name: Roman numerals I V X
roman-iview.phrase: I View Xylophones: I=1, V=5, X=10 (extend: L=50, C=100, D=500, M=1000).
roman-iview.also: I View X-rays works too for the first three.
steps: Learn the seven symbols: I=1, V=5, X=10, L=50, C=100, D=500, M=1000.
Read left to right, adding values.
Apply subtractive pairs when a smaller symbol sits before a larger one.
roman-iview.exception: Subtractive notation: IV=4, IX=9, XL=40, XC=90, CD=400, CM=900.

commute3.name: Commutative multiply
steps: Use the order you know better.
commute3.exception: Arrays look different when swapped (2×6 vs 6×2) but count the same dots.

assoc3.name: Associative multiply
assoc3.exception: Only regroup — don’t drop a factor.

distrib3.name: Distributive property
distrib3.phrase: Break a hard times into two easy times, then add.
steps: Split one factor into friendly parts.
distrib3.exception: Split into a sum (or difference), not a product — that’s a different rule.

wordkeys3.name: Word-problem keywords
steps: Pick the operation it usually signals.
Write the number sentence and solve.
wordkeys3.exception: Keywords help but the story wins — “each” can divide when sharing.

estimate3.name: Estimate products
estimate3.phrase: Round, then multiply — about how many?
steps: Round each factor to a friendly number.
estimate3.exception: Rounding both up overestimates. Good for checking ballpark, not exact answers.

gallon.name: Gallon Man
gallon.phrase: King Gallon had 4 quarts; each quart 2 pints; each pint 2 cups.
gallon.also: 4 quarts = 1 gallon. 2 pints = 1 quart. 2 cups = 1 pint.
gallon.exception: US liquid measures. Don’t mix with liters without converting.

kinghenry3.name: King Henry metric
kinghenry3.phrase: King Henry Died By Drinking Chocolate Milk.
kinghenry3.also: Kilo, Hecto, Deca, Base, Deci, Centi, Milli — each step is ×10 or ÷10.
steps: Line up the King Henry words with prefixes.
Move the decimal that many places.
kinghenry3.exception: “By” is the base unit. Mega/micro/nano are off this ladder. Each hop is ×10 or ÷10. Miles and inches need different bridges.

zeroprop.name: Zero and one in multiply
zeroprop.phrase: Times zero wipes out. Times one keeps it.
zeroprop.exception: Adding zero keeps n; multiplying by zero does not.

remain3.name: Remainders
remain3.phrase: Divide until you can’t make another full group — what’s left is the remainder.
steps: Divide for how many full groups.
Subtract from the total — that leftover is R.
remain3.exception: Remainder must be smaller than the divisor. If not, you can make another group.

array3.name: Arrays
array3.phrase: Rows times columns — an array shows multiply.
steps: Count how many in each row.
array3.exception: A scattered pile is not an array until you line it into equal rows.

tomatoes.name: Feet in a mile
tomatoes.phrase: Silly optional hook: “five tomatoes” sounds like 5-2-8-0 (feet in a mile).
steps: Check the real fact: 5,280 feet per mile.
tomatoes.exception: Not a math procedure — a joke scaffold with no structure. Digits scramble easily; verify 5,280 feet per mile.

orderops3.name: × before +
orderops3.phrase: My Dear before Aunt Sally: multiply before you add.
orderops3.also: A early peek at order of operations.
orderops3.exception: Brackets still beat everything. × and ÷ tie left to right when both appear; without brackets, ×÷ beat +−.

northdakota.name: Numerator & denominator
northdakota.phrase: Nice Dog: Numerator up, Denominator down. N before D.
steps: N before D in the alphabet — top before bottom in the name.
northdakota.exception: The bar means divide: top ÷ bottom, not bottom ÷ top.

mental3.name: Mental math: ×10 and ×100
mental3.phrase: ×10 adds a zero. ×100 adds two zeros.
steps: For ×10, write a zero on the end.
mental3.exception: For decimals the zeros work differently — digits slide across the point.

patterns3.name: Number patterns
patterns3.phrase: Find the jump rule, then keep jumping.
steps: Subtract neighbors to find the jump.
Apply the jump to find the next term.
patterns3.exception: Some patterns change rule (square numbers). These drills stay on constant jumps.
